@common.attachEmailPlaceholder.sameAsSourceJustification: Example email address “you@example.com”: a recognizable placeholder shape whose @-pattern is what hints “email”. Apple keeps example addresses in this Latin form in its Traditional Chinese localizations too, so translating it would make the hint less readable, not more.

@common.sizeUnit.kibibyte.sameAsSourceJustification: Traditional Chinese keeps the IEC binary symbols in Latin: KDE Dolphin zh-TW writes ` MiB` untranslated, and the Microsoft zh-Hant terminology keeps `GiB` as is. There is no Han symbol to localize; only the bare byte word is translated (`common.sizeUnit.byte` = `位元組`).

@common.sizeUnit.kilobyte.sameAsSourceJustification: Traditional Chinese writes byte-multiple unit symbols in Latin (macOS zh-TW and zh-HK, Microsoft zh-Hant, TC zh-TW). The SI lowercase k is kept so the decimal kilobyte stays distinct from the binary `KiB`; macOS and Microsoft write the decimal unit as `KB`, which here would blur with the old binary meaning.

@common.sizeUnit.megabyte.sameAsSourceJustification: Traditional Chinese writes byte-multiple unit symbols in Latin, as macOS zh-TW and zh-HK Finder do (pile: `KB`, `MB`, `GB`, `TB`, `PB` beside the translated `位元組`; TC zh-TW `位元組|KB|MB|GB`). Microsoft zh-Hant does the same. There is no Han symbol to localize; only the bare byte word is translated (`common.sizeUnit.byte` = `位元組`).
